A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TEASR, with matching authors, method and original experiments. Text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. The supplied v1 ends after references; v2 includes an additional readable supplementary section.

before.justification: v1 reports original super-resolution results on RealSR, DRealSR and DIV2K-Val, along with sampling-step comparisons and DTC/TAR ablations in Tables 1–3.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original efficiency measurements, TAR sensitivity results, training curves and qualitative training-stability analyses.

M1.justification: The SAD framework, dual-branch DTC architecture, TAR weighting, reconstruction objectives and any-step inference procedure are retained. The new supplementary training algorithm and loss-weight details document implementation without establishing a redesign of the proposed method.

E1.justification: Training still uses LSDIR and FFHQ, while evaluation retains RealSR, DRealSR and DIV2K-Val for super-resolution. The Z-Image experiments change backbone configuration, and additional visual examples do not establish a new dataset, domain or task.

E2.justification: The original Table 1 comparator set is retained. New efficiency comparisons include DMD, ADD and SFT on Z-Image (main Figure 5), and PiSA-SR in supplementary Table 1. Supplementary Figure 2 also adds a DiT4SR curve and OSEDiff reference point to the sampling-budget comparison, substantially broadening evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 adds common-backbone Z-Image-6B/A100 memory and iteration-time benchmarking, inference latency measurements, and training-memory tests specifying 512×512 inputs, batch size 1 and checkpointing. Original accuracy protocols remain unchanged. Supplementary Algorithm 2 specifies rectification timesteps U(0.05,0.95), differing from U(0,1) in both versions' main text; this reporting discrepancy does not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained DTC/TAR ablations, v2 adds an intermediate TAR schedule, comparative sampling-budget analysis, loss curves, and early-training visualizations of one-step estimates and fake trajectories. It also examines applicability to a smaller backbone. These provide substantial new evidence about schedule sensitivity, training stability and low-step behavior.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random-seed studies, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added loss curves describe training dynamics rather than uncertainty across independent runs.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in the original benchmark, sampling and ablation tables are unchanged. Substantial new results include Z-Image training memory of 31.8 GB for TEASR versus 65.6 GB for ADD, with iteration times of 3.8 versus 2.1 seconds; inference costs; and additional TAR, sampling and training-stability outcomes. These are added measurements, not improvements to the original accuracy scores.

T1.justification: v1 motivates TAR's existing weight (1-s)^2/s through noise-dependent guidance reliability. Supplementary Section 4 in v2 adds a mathematical derivation connecting KL divergence, score differences, flow velocities and the stop-gradient rectification objective. This substantially expands the theoretical treatment without introducing a different TAR weight.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims: single-model self-adversarial distillation, reduced training-memory requirements, DTC/TAR, and flexible one-to-many-step restoration. New efficiency and supplementary evidence supports these existing claims rather than redefining the main contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of smaller-backbone applicability, stable early adversarial learning, and TAR's weighting as arising from distribution matching. It also clarifies the distinction between flexible standard-diffusion sampling and useful low-step restoration. The main limitations concerning model capacity and independent fidelity–realism control remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The supplement adds training pseudocode, the combined loss and timestep-dependent loss weights, sampling distributions, bfloat16 precision, checkpointing, and the precise 47,496-iteration count. The abstract adds a code-repository link. These substantially expand reproducibility information beyond v1's shorter optimizer, LoRA and hardware description; the link alone does not verify resource availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations covering PiSA-SR, controllable and time-aware one-step SR, and adjacent restoration/generation work. It newly contrasts TAR with multi-forward averaging and fixed-timestep approaches. The central positioning relative to TwinFlow, FACM and distribution matching remains intact; duplicate consolidation and publication updates do not constitute new cited work.

P1.justification: The existing narrative and section organization are largely retained, with localized introduction and TAR rewrites, terminology clarifications, corrected author/running headers, and acknowledgments. An efficiency subsection and organized supplement are added, but the original paper is not extensively rewritten or reorganized.

P2.justification: v2 adds efficiency charts and tables, a hyperparameter table, training pseudocode, loss plots, a comparative sampling plot, training-progression images and extensive qualitative grids. Original displays are retained, with several relocated or renumbered. The new visual presentation is substantial beyond pagination changes.

improvement.justification: v1 supports its central training-efficiency claim largely through model counts. v2 adds measured costs, including a common-backbone comparison, concrete 20B-model memory requirements, detailed training documentation, and targeted sensitivity and stability evidence. These substantially strengthen validation and reproducibility while retaining the original results. The measurements reveal a memory–iteration-time tradeoff, and the main-text/algorithm timestep discrepancy remains a reproducibility issue, but these limitations do not outweigh the gains.
